messages.subject: inla.spde2.pcmatern hyperparameters do not match fitted/predicted surface
parts:
Dear all,

I recently ran into the following problem when I tried to run some inla models for spatial data.

I have two latent components s1 and s2 with alpha fixed to 3/2, and their parameter estimates (median) are:

s1 range = 1633, s2 range = 530
s1 sd = 0.18, s2 sd = 0.51
my spatial domain is about 50000 by 50000.

The two problems:

sd(mod$summary.random$s1$`0.5quant`) = 0.08
sd(mod$summary.random$s2$`0.5quant`) = 0.03

-- while I don't expect they should match the hyperparameter estimates, I don't know why the sd of s2 median estimates at mesh points are smaller than s1


pred.loc <- spsample(mydomain, 5000, type = "random")
preds <- inla.mesh.project(inla.mesh.projector(mesh.point, loc = pred.loc@coords), mod$summary.random$s1$`0.5quant`) # project to random locations
pred.w1 <- SpatialPointsDataFrame(pred.loc, data.frame(w1 = preds))
plot(variogram(w1~1, pred.w1, cutoff = 10000)) # calculates sample variogram values 


-- the empirical variogram also does not match the hyperparameter estimates of s1 (and s2), the practical range looks to be around 4000, and partial sill is only 0.006

What’s the max.edge setting for the mesh? If the triangles are too large there will be bias in the parameter estimates.

With multiple likelihood’s and copy models, I would expect complex interaction of information flow between the models.

To check properly, you may need to run the estimation on simulated data, to see if it recovers the true parameters (or similar, since there is no guarantees in a single-realisation model...)

Finn

Hi,
So the estimated ranges are smaller than, or on the same order as, the triangle edges.
That should result in bias in the variance parameters estimates, so that might explain the results you see; the interpretation of the variance parameter simply doesn’t hold when the triangles are too large.  I believe we discussed/illustrated this a bit in the discussion part of the Lindgren et al 2011 JRSSB read paper on the link between SPDEs and GMRFs.

Finn
